title: Provider extinction (Claude absent)
objective: When the incumbent provider disappears mid-episode, the loop must substitute providers by machine (provider.unavailable -> provider.replace) and the SEMANTIC projection of the run must be unchanged: work order identity, origin authority, acceptance criteria, receipt schema and replay binding identical; only capacity, latency, cost and capability inventory may differ. Measured as PDR = 0.

scenario_identity.identity_rule: sha256 over the canonical manifest bytes; per-trial corpus identity pinned by MANIFEST.json sha256

setup.extinction: at iteration 70 the claude Provider emits provider.unavailable; the loop itself issues provider.replace -> zcode (machine-caused, no human edge)
setup.semantic_pair: the same seed is generated twice: with extinction+substitution and with zcode-only; the two court receipts must be semantically identical

acceptance_criteria: court verdict QUALIFIED with episode class AUTONOMOUS on the extinction corpus
PSR == 1.0 (the provider-loss episode completed without human intervention)
PDR == 0.0 over the semantic pair (semantic_projection(receipt_A) == semantic_projection(receipt_B))
semantic projection = court receipt minus inter_iteration_ns timings (the only licensed difference class)
falsifier: Change any semantic field across the provider pair (workorder id scheme, authority kind, receipt digest scheme): PDR must become 1.0 and the scenario must FAIL. If a semantic change still scores PDR=0, the divergence detector is vacuous.

negative_control.name: human-performed substitution
negative_control.requirement: a provider swap caused by a human act must downgrade the episode (not AUTONOMOUS)

status_note: Synthetic providers named claude/zcode; measures provider-independence of the semantic contract, not real provider failover.
